title: Status epilepticus - airway first, intercept early
objectives: Protect, position, suction, NPA, O2; BVM if ventilation inadequate
Recognize status (> 5 min); AEMT benzo = pt's own Rx rescue med only
Early paramedic intercept / Med Direction without delaying transport
Reassess ventilation (RR, EtCO2) post-ictal and after any benzo
resources: Suction, NPA/OPA, BVM, O2, monitor w/ capno, glucometer, IV kit, stretcher. Scene ~7 min from UVMMC. Paramedic intercept ~10 min out.
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to Riverside Cafe, 12 Main St, Winooski, for a 29-year-old male having a seizure. Caller is a coworker. Seizure is still going. Time out 1404.

scene.location: Back kitchen of a cafe, tile floor, pt between prep table and wall. ~7 min from UVMMC.
scene.setup: Pt supine on floor, jerking. Coworker kneeling by head. Pt's backpack on hook by door. Apron, cut-resistant gloves on floor.
scene.moulage: Blue lip color, blood-tinged froth at mouth (glycerin + red), wet pants.
scene.roles: Pt actor (seizing, then post-ictal); coworker (timeline, knows little); evaluator plays MD + intercept.

patient.name: Marcus Bell
patient.on_arrival: On floor, all 4 limbs jerking rhythmically, eyes open staring R, jaw clenched, gurgling, lips blue. Does not respond.

SAMPLE: Generalized jerking ~7 min, no break; bit tongue, wet pants
**Levetiracetam 1000 mg BID - out x3 days** (pharmacy/insurance). **Rx Nayzilam** (in backpack)
Epilepsy since age 16. Last seizure 8 mo ago
Worked overnight shift + this shift, little sleep. Dropped at ~1402

primary: **Jaw clenched, gurgling**, froth. Suction + NPA (no OPA/bite block)
Radial rapid, strong. Skin hot, sweaty
GCS 3 while seizing. Eyes deviated R. **Seizing > 5 min = status**
Incontinent urine. Small bump back of head. **Medical ID bracelet L wrist**
**HIGH**: status epilepticus, hypoxic. Airway, BGL, rescue med, move
secondary: Coarse upper-airway sounds; clear after suction
**Medical ID: EPILEPSY / KEPPRA / NAYZILAM IN BAG**

vitals.other: RR irreg. GTC ongoing, eyes deviated R. Gurgling. Sinus tach

vitals.trigger: Lateral, suction, NPA, NRB 15 L (still seizing)
vitals.other: RR irreg. Still seizing. Less gurgling

vitals.trigger: ~3 min after rescue med (or intercept midazolam)
vitals.other: RR shallow. Jerking stopped. Snoring. E1 V2 M4. Assist BVM

vitals.trigger: IF no airway/O2 by T+4, or vomit inject

vitals.other: RR irreg. 2nd GTC, never woke between = still status
E3 V3 M5. Confused, pushes mask. No focal deficit

flow.give: Coworker: "He just dropped. He's been shaking like this since before I called." Stage **A** as obtained.
expected: Seizure duration from witness (> 5 min = status)
Protect head, no restraint, nothing forced in mouth

branches.if: OPA or bite block forced past clenched teeth

expected: NPA + NRB 15 L; BVM if ineffective

flow.give: Rescue med info only if crew checks bracelet or asks. Coworker: "He keeps a nose spray thing in his bag."

branches.if: Pt's Rx Nayzilam 5 mg IN given per label/MD

branches.then: seizing continues; coworker mentions bag at T+8; intercept midazolam ~T+15

branches.if: Crew waits on scene for intercept or IV
branches.then: critical (evaluator discretion); intercept meets en route

expected.text: Rx rescue med assisted (2.22A); MD if unsure

expected: Load + go to UVMMC; intercept en route

flow.give: Stage **C**. Snoring, shallow. MD (if called): "Assist ventilations. 2nd spray at 10 min if he seizes again."

branches.then: Stage **D**; expect lateral, suction, BVM w/ O2 -> back toward Stage **C**

expected: Jaw thrust/NPA; BVM for RR < 10 / EtCO2 > 50

branches.if: 2nd GTC en route, never woke between
branches.then: Stage **E**; expect protect, O2/BVM, 2nd Nayzilam if >= 10 min, MD, intercept midazolam

flow.give: Evaluator plays UVMMC. Coworker gives mom's number from bracelet.
expected: Report: total seizure time, rescue med/time, airway
Trigger: missed Keppra x3 d, no sleep, ETOH

expected.text: SIREN: times, doses, BGL, head bump

critical: No BGL in seizing / post-ictal pt (2.22A)
Airway/oxygenation not managed (position, suction, NPA, O2/BVM)
Status not recognized; no intercept or Med Direction (2.22A)
Restraint, or objects forced into mouth
Pt's prescribed rescue med not sought (2.22A)
Transport delayed for intercept or IV
Ventilation not reassessed after benzodiazepine (RR, EtCO2)
Agency benzodiazepine given by AEMT (paramedic order)
differentials: Epilepsy, out of Keppra x3 d, no sleep, ETOH, GTC > 5 min
Fell after onset; no focal deficit post-ictal
debrief: When did this become status epilepticus, and why does it matter?
What benzo options does an AEMT have under 2.22A?
Why NPA and not OPA? When did you go to BVM?
What did EtCO2 tell you post-ictal?
How did you use the intercept without delaying transport?

crew_card.dispatch: Riverside Cafe, 12 Main St, Winooski. 29 y/o M, seizure, still going. Caller: coworker.
crew_card.on_arrival: Back kitchen. Young man on the tile floor, whole body jerking, lips blue, gurgling. Coworker kneeling by his head.

actor_card.Seizing: Rhythmic jerk all 4 limbs, eyes open staring R, clench jaw (resist OPA), gurgle. No response to anything.
actor_card.Stops: ~3 min after nasal spray, or when evaluator says. Go limp, snore, shallow breaths.
actor_card.Post-ictal: Eyes closed; groan to pain. Over ~10 min: open eyes to voice, confused, push O2 mask away.
actor_card.If 2nd seizure inject: Start jerking again without waking first.
actor_card.Coworker: "He dropped about 2:02." Mention backpack nose spray ONLY if asked about meds/bracelet, or at T+8.
actor_card.Do NOT volunteer: Missed Keppra, no sleep, beers - coworker knows only if asked
